text: Human Rights Watch reports that there was minimal accountability for the rights violations committed by Kazakh law enforcement during and immediately after the deadly January 2022 anti-government protests, with only a handful of officials prosecuted for torture and ill-treatment of detainees; Kazakh authorities also routinely violate the rights to peaceful assembly, freedom of expression and freedom of association, and courts have imprisoned government critics and journalists on overbroad extremism and false-information charges.
short: Minimal accountability for killings and torture around Kazakhstan's deadly January 2022 protests; critics and journalists imprisoned.

source.name: Human Rights Watch, World Report 2025: Kazakhstan (events of 2024)
source.quote: There continued to be minimal accountability for law enforcement officials for rights violations perpetrated during and immediately after deadly 2022 anti-government protests.
source.note: Same chapter: 'A handful of law enforcement officials were prosecuted in 2024 for torture and ill-treatment of detainees'; the keynote opens 'Authorities in Kazakhstan routinely violate the rights to peaceful assembly, freedom of expression, and freedom of association'.

additionalSources.name: Amnesty International, Report 2025/26 — Kazakhstan
additionalSources.quote: Impunity persisted for the majority of serious human rights violations committed during the January 2022 protests.
additionalSources.note: Same report: at least 39 people imprisoned on politically motivated charges during the year; the OSCE/ODIHR noted a 'stark disparity between the high number of civilian deaths, widespread allegations of torture and ill-treatment and the low number of prosecutions for these killings'.
